findings.title: Meta disputes claim that Muse read a user's private messages without permission
findings.summary_md: Meta vice president Andy Stone said the Messages integration in the Muse app for Mac is opt-in and requires both Full Disk Access and the Messages connector before Muse can read Messages content. The statement answered Inc. columnist Jason Aten's report that Muse had read his private messages without permission. TechCrunch reported that Meta rejected the claim that its product did this without the user's consent.

findings.title: Updates to Full Disk Access in macOS
findings.summary_md: Apple said Full Disk Access largely sidesteps macOS privacy controls so backup apps can work, and that some developers use it in ways that expose files, mail, messages, and browsing history without users' full knowledge. Apple added that this can compromise the privacy of people communicating with those users. The company said it would introduce additional controls requiring very explicit user action, citing the growing capability and autonomy of AI agents.

findings.title: A Flaw in ChatGPT's Mac App Could Have Let Hackers Grab Sensitive Data
findings.summary_md: Objective-See Foundation researchers found a patched flaw in the macOS ChatGPT app that could let an attacker take over the app and reach its chat logs, other stored data, and interconnections such as browser sessions. Researcher Patrick Wardle said agents need broad access and become a high-value target when that access can be subverted. OpenAI acknowledged the flaw and fix in its system change log on September 25, according to WIRED.

findings.title: Apple says it's tightening macOS 'Full Disk Access' controls due to new risks from AI agents
findings.summary_md: Apple announced additional controls around the macOS Full Disk Access setting days after the Muse messages claim and a WIRED report on a ChatGPT Mac app flaw. TechCrunch noted that the setting was designed to let backups function properly while AI agents increase the risk of broad access. Apple warned that granting it puts all data on a Mac at risk.

findings.title: Apple says it's tightening macOS privacy controls amid the rise of AI agents
findings.summary_md: 9to5Mac reported that Apple planned changes to macOS Full Disk Access amid AI agents requesting that permission. The article said Apple had not shared specifics of the planned controls beyond requiring very explicit user action. It framed the move as a privacy response to the rapid rise of autonomous AI agents on Macs.
